gen-zen-dots-gf-cascadia-mono: Cascadia Mono stands its letters like pins in a wide board. Zen Dots lends the heading a friendly techy spaciousness, and the body's compact, monoline skyline gives that room something tidy to push against.
gen-zen-dots-gf-julius-sans-one: Friendly, a little techy: that's Zen Dots up top. Julius Sans One follows with wide gaps between letters and open-ended curves, so both fonts leave plenty of room on the page.
gen-zen-dots-gf-lexend-exa: Friendly, techy shapes lead in Zen Dots. Lexend Exa brings wide-open curves and a tall x-height against the heading's moderate lowercase, and that difference in height is what makes the pair distinct.
gen-zen-dots-gf-lexend-giga: Techy and friendly, Zen Dots leaves space around every letter. Lexend Giga then glides along on flat, generously tracked lines, so whole paragraphs move light and unhurried under the eye.
gen-zen-dots-gf-lexend-mega: Lexend Mega draws every letter with a single nib. Zen Dots does best at making a spacious, techy first impression, while Lexend Mega is built for carrying words at a height close to the capitals.
gen-zen-dots-gf-lexend-peta: Friendly and techy, Zen Dots takes the lead. Where the heading excels at spacious, techy display, Lexend Peta does its best work with unthinning curves and a large x-height.
gen-zen-dots-gf-lexend-tera: Zen Dots gives every letter generous room, with openings that stay wide at every weight. But Lexend Tera spaces its letters like stepping stones, so paragraphs move along in a single plotted line.
gen-zen-dots-gf-lexend-zetta: Zen Dots leaves generous room around every letter, which gives its display shapes a friendly, techy feel. Lexend Zetta takes the quieter job, setting tall-bodied small letters in widely tracked ribbons of constant width.
gen-zen-dots-gf-montserrat-alternates: Montserrat Alternates has a c as open as a bent paperclip. Zen Dots is the one for making an entrance, spacious and techy, while the body font quietly crowds its lowercase up toward the capital line.
gen-zen-dots-newsreader: Zen Dots brings friendly, techy shapes with generous room around every letter. And Newsreader, with restrained stroke contrast and open curves, carries paragraphs from line to line with quiet authority.
